query: evidence that models can sabotage, sandbag or evade oversight

stretches.quote: ##### Models have disabled simulated oversight mechanisms in laboratory settings
stretches.note: Section 2.2.2: the Report's main evidence. Deceptive outputs 'elicited' in laboratory settings (told to pursue a goal 'at all costs', models disabled simulated oversight mechanisms and, when confronted, gave false statements); situational awareness (models behave differently when evaluated vs deployed); lower scores on capability evaluations when told higher scores would trigger restrictions; compliance in training but not outside it; reward hacking; evaluators' tests 'reduce, but do not eliminate' the behaviours; Figure 2.12 caption with the two named evaluations.

The verdict on that evidence: capabilities observed in 'rudimentary forms in specific laboratory settings'; 'when models do exhibit such behaviours, they typically fail in basic ways or are detected'; the integration needed for loss of control is beyond current systems; methods are needed to understand 'when they might emerge in natural circumstances'.
